requirement:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.
#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.
**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Getting the stack trace.** Console output truncates the exception to its message; `-p:ErrorLog=out.sarif` preserves the full description, including the stack trace and an `ISymbol:` context line naming the offending type:

```
dotnet build -p:ErrorLog=out.sarif
```

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

story.summary: The change stops the MessagePack source generator and analyzer from crashing when a `[MessagePackObject]` member's type is a closed generic value type from a referenced assembly. Two diagnostic sites in `TypeCollector` no longer index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]`. One now uses `FirstOrDefault()` and the other a new null-safe helper. Every analyzer diagnostic now also passes through a new filter that drops any diagnostic whose location is not a source tree in the current compilation. Three tests compile a library to a metadata-only image and check that no warnings come out and that the resolver is generated. README and the MsgPack004 doc gain notes on the new behaviour.
story.why: For metadata symbols, `DeclaringSyntaxReferences` is empty, so `[0]` threw `IndexOutOfRangeException`. The generator then emitted no resolver at all, which breaks trimmed and NativeAOT apps at runtime. The fix at line 1077 matters for the generator too, because that `Diagnostic` is built even when `reportDiagnostic` is null.
touches_beyond_requirement: A global diagnostic filter (line 239, lines 1444-1450) silently drops every analyzer diagnostic without an in-compilation source location, including `Location.None` ones, not just the ones for metadata types.
The cast at line 985 changed from a hard cast to `as PropertyDeclarationSyntax`. This changes behaviour for source-declared positional record properties too.
New README section and new MsgPack004.md section describing diagnostic ownership for referenced types.
story.confidence_overview: Medium confidence that the repro is fixed: the tests mirror the issue's repro and check that the resolver exists. The issue names a third indexing site (old line 735) that the diff does not touch; it may or may not still crash on other shapes. The new filter has wider effects than the bug needs.

claims.text: The BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic now gets its location from a null-safe helper rather than `[0]` plus a hard cast.
claims.requirement_quote: Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly

claims.text: The new docs state that diagnostics for members of referenced types are reported by the defining project, not the consumer.

The MemberNeedsKey diagnostic is built with `DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?` instead of `[0]`. This removes the crash for metadata members, in both the generator and the analyzer, since this `Diagnostic` is created unconditionally.
claims.requirement_quote: Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()`

claims.text: Analyzer diagnostics are reported only when their location is in a source tree of the current compilation; all others are silently dropped.

The tests reproduce the issue's shape. They cover a generic struct and a positional generic record struct compiled into a metadata-only image and used as a member type. They fail on any diagnostic, assert no warning-or-higher generator diagnostics, and assert the resolver hint name is generated.
claims.requirement_quote: Expected behavior: A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

claims.text: The tests use `MetadataReference.CreateFromImage` on an emitted assembly, so the referenced type truly has no syntax. This matches the issue's point that the crash is specific to metadata symbols.
claims.requirement_quote: which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols

claims.text: Scope: the only product code changed is private code in TypeCollector.cs. No public API, analyzer rule descriptors or wire format were changed. Two documentation files were also edited.

refusals.what: The global filter changes which analyzer diagnostics users see: any diagnostic without an in-compilation source location is now suppressed.
refusals.why: This is a user-visible change to analyzer behaviour beyond fixing the crash. It may hide diagnostics that previously appeared with no location.

refusals.what: The README and MsgPack004 doc edits promise that diagnostics for referenced types are handled by the defining assembly.
refusals.why: These are documentation changes beyond the requirement, and the guarantee does not hold when the defining assembly lacks the analyzer.

findings.description: The issue lists three `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites (old lines 735, 1009, 1101). The diff has no hunk near line 735, so that site appears unchanged. If it is still an unguarded `[0]`, other type shapes from metadata (beyond the three tested) may still crash. This cannot be verified from the diff.

The filter drops every diagnostic whose location is `Location.None` or not in source. That includes diagnostics for source types whose location helper happens to return null. Before this change such diagnostics were reported with no location; now they vanish silently. This can hide real user errors in the consuming project.

Positional record properties are declared by a `ParameterSyntax`, not a `PropertyDeclarationSyntax`. For such a property in source with no key, the `as` cast returns null. The resulting `Location.None` diagnostic is then dropped by the filter, so BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull is silently suppressed for source code. The old hard cast would have thrown instead. No test covers this path.

The doc says problems are "reported by the assembly that defines it". That only holds if the defining project also runs the MessagePack analyzer, which a third-party NuGet package may not. Consumers may therefore get no warning about unkeyed members that affect serialization.

It is not visible whether `VerifyCS` (`CSharpSourceGeneratorVerifier<MessagePackGenerator>`) also runs `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer`. If it does not, the AD0001 half of the bug is not exercised by these tests.

out_of_scope.description: New section "Generic types from referenced assemblies" documenting diagnostic ownership. The bug fix does not need it.
New section stating that the analyzer only reports on members declared in the project being compiled.
The global `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` filter applies to all analyzer diagnostics, not only those for metadata types.
